meta.name: Grain-Free Bread
meta.description: A nut-flour loaf using almond flour, coconut flour, and whipped egg whites for structure. No wheat, no yeast, no sugar. Psyllium husk provides the elastic network that gluten normally would.

change_log.summary: Initial recipe from food science research synthesis — almond/coconut flour blend with psyllium husk binder, dual leavening (whipped whites + baking powder)

ingredients.name: Blanched Almond Flour (superfine)
ingredients.rationale: Provides bulk and lighter texture. Must be blanched and superfine — almond meal is too coarse and heavy.

ingredients.name: Coconut Flour
ingredients.rationale: Absorbs excess oil from almond flour, provides fiber. Contains 60.9% dietary fiber — absorbs 4-5x its weight in liquid.

ingredients.name: Psyllium Husk Powder
ingredients.rationale: The gluten mimic — forms elastic gel network, increases gas-holding capacity from 84% to 98.5%. Pre-hydration essential.

ingredients.name: Warm Water
ingredients.rationale: For psyllium pre-hydration. Warm water accelerates gel formation.

ingredients.name: Large Eggs
ingredients.rationale: 4 eggs separated. Whites provide mechanical leavening (6-8x volume). Yolks contribute flavor, color, and emulsification.

ingredients.name: Cream of Tartar
ingredients.rationale: Stabilizes egg white foam — without it, foam collapses after ~5 minutes.

ingredients.name: Baking Powder (double-acting)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Section 6 research — double-acting preferred over baking soda alone
ingredients.rationale: Releases CO2 in two phases (wet + heat). Combined with ACV for extra acid activation.

ingredients.name: Apple Cider Vinegar
ingredients.rationale: Activates leavening, weakens protein bonds for tender crumb, masks eggy flavor.

ingredients.name: Fine Sea Salt
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Standard baker's percentage adjusted for grain-free
ingredients.rationale: ~1.3% of total flour weight. Enhances flavor and strengthens egg protein structure.

ingredients.name: Unsalted Butter (melted)
ingredients.rationale: Minimal added fat — almond flour is already ~50% fat. Adds flavor and moisture.

ingredients.name: Xanthan Gum
ingredients.rationale: Provides gas-trapping film alongside psyllium's elasticity. ATK says xanthan behaves most like gluten of all replacers.

states.title: Prepare Workspace
states.direction: Gather all vessels, equipment, and ingredients. Melt butter. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line the loaf pan with parchment paper or grease thoroughly.
states.exit_condition: Oven preheating, loaf pan prepared, all ingredients and equipment laid out

notes.text: Use blanched, superfine almond flour — not almond meal. Almond meal has skins and is coarser, deflating egg white foam faster.
Eggs must be room temperature — room temp whites whip to greater volume than cold.

states.title: Separate Eggs
states.direction: Separate 4 large eggs. Place whites (132g) in the large clean grease-free bowl (V3). Set yolks (68g) aside in a small cup. Ensure no yolk contaminates the whites.
states.exit_condition: 4 whites in V3 (no yolk contamination), 4 yolks set aside

notes.text: Separate eggs one at a time over a small bowl first, then transfer clean whites to V3. One broken yolk ruins the whole batch — even a trace of fat prevents whipping.

states.title: Mix Psyllium with Warm Water
states.direction: In the medium bowl (V2), add 14g psyllium husk powder. Pour in 90g warm water and stir vigorously until combined. The mixture will thicken rapidly into a gel.
states.exit_condition: Psyllium and water are fully combined, beginning to gel

notes.text: If using whole psyllium husks instead of powder, use DOUBLE the amount (28g). Powder absorbs faster.

states.title: Rest Psyllium Gel
states.direction: Let the psyllium mixture rest for 5 minutes to fully hydrate and form a thick, stretchy gel.
states.exit_condition: Psyllium has formed a thick, stretchy gel — 5 minutes elapsed

states.title: Whisk Dry Ingredients
states.direction: In the large mixing bowl (V1), whisk together 168g almond flour, 56g coconut flour, 7g baking powder, 3g salt, and 1g xanthan gum until evenly combined.
states.exit_condition: Dry ingredients evenly combined, no visible clumps

states.title: Combine Wet Ingredients
states.direction: To the psyllium gel in V2, add the 4 egg yolks, 28g melted butter, and 5g apple cider vinegar. Stir until smooth.
states.exit_condition: Wet ingredients are smooth and homogeneous, gel fully incorporated

states.title: Combine Wet into Dry
states.direction: Pour the wet mixture from V2 into the dry ingredients in V1. Stir with a rubber spatula until just combined — a thick, heavy batter.
states.exit_condition: Batter is uniformly mixed with no dry pockets

notes.text: The batter will be much heavier and thicker than wheat bread batter. This is normal — the egg whites will lighten it.

states.title: Rest Batter
states.direction: Let the batter rest for 5 minutes. Coconut flour continues absorbing moisture after mixing — the batter will thicken noticeably.
states.exit_condition: 5 minutes elapsed, batter has thickened as coconut flour hydrates

notes.text: If batter is too thick after resting, add warm water 1 tablespoon at a time. If too thin, add 1 tablespoon coconut flour.

states.title: Whip Egg Whites to Stiff Peaks
states.direction: Using a hand mixer or stand mixer, beat the 4 egg whites in V3 on low speed to create small bubbles. Add 0.5g cream of tartar. Increase to medium-high and beat until stiff peaks — the foam holds its shape when the whisk is lifted.
states.exit_condition: Stiff peaks — foam holds shape, tips stand straight up, bowl can be inverted

notes.text: Start slow, then increase speed. Over-beaten whites break into dry chunks when folded — stop at stiff peaks, not dry peaks.
Once whites are whipped, fold immediately. Foam starts collapsing after 5 minutes.

states.title: Fold Whites — First Addition
states.direction: Add about half the whipped egg whites to the batter in V1. Mix aggressively with the spatula to lighten the heavy batter. Expect to lose about 50% of this volume — that's intentional.
states.exit_condition: First half incorporated, batter is noticeably lighter

states.title: Fold Whites — Second Addition
states.direction: Add remaining whipped whites. Fold gently — cut down through center, sweep along bottom, fold over top. Rotate bowl a quarter turn and repeat. Preserve as much air as possible.
states.exit_condition: Whites fully incorporated with no white streaks, batter is light and airy

notes.text: A few small streaks of white are better than over-folding. Stop as soon as the batter is mostly uniform.

states.title: Fill Loaf Pan
states.direction: Gently pour the batter into the prepared loaf pan (V4). Smooth the top with the spatula. Optionally brush the surface with beaten egg yolk for better browning.
states.exit_condition: Batter in pan with smooth, even top

notes.text: Get into the oven within 2-3 minutes. The chemical leavening reaction is fast — delay means lost gas.

states.title: Bake
states.direction: Bake at 350°F (175°C) on the middle rack for 45-55 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean and internal temperature reaches 200-205°F (93-96°C).
states.exit_condition: Toothpick clean, internal temp 200-205°F (93-96°C), top is golden brown

notes.text: If top browns too quickly, tent with foil after 30 minutes.
Internal temp MUST reach 200°F (93°C) for complete starch gelatinization. Under-baked = gummy interior.

states.title: Cool in Pan
states.direction: Remove from oven. Let bread cool in the pan for 10 minutes. The structure is fragile when hot.
states.exit_condition: 10 minutes in pan, bread has firmed slightly

states.title: Cool on Wire Rack
states.direction: Carefully remove from pan and place on a wire rack. Cool at least 30 minutes before slicing. The egg flavor mellows significantly as the bread cools.
states.exit_condition: Bread cooled at least 30 minutes, no longer warm to the touch

notes.text: Do not slice until completely cool. Starches are still setting — cutting early = gummy interior.

reminders.prompt: Rate crumb texture (dense, cakey, or bread-like?)

methods.detail: Slice and toast directly — grain-free bread reheats best this way.
Room temp in airtight container for 2-3 days. Freeze sliced in zip-lock for up to 2 weeks.

techniques.name: 3:1 almond-to-coconut flour ratio
techniques.sourcedFrom: Atkins, The Coconut Mama, Panhandle Milling
techniques.rationale: Most recommended blend. Coconut flour absorbs excess oil from almond flour; almond provides bulk and lighter texture.

techniques.name: Psyllium husk pre-hydration
techniques.sourcedFrom: PMC peer-reviewed study, Gluten Free Alchemist
techniques.rationale: Gel network must form before adding to batter to trap gas. Pre-hydrate in warm water for 5 minutes.

techniques.name: Separated eggs with whipped whites
techniques.sourcedFrom: Flavor Insider, Pastry Chef Online, Gluten Free on a Shoestring
techniques.rationale: Whipped whites provide mechanical leavening. More reliable than chemical leavening in grain-free systems.

techniques.name: Dual leavening (mechanical + chemical)
techniques.rationale: Whipped whites for primary rise, baking powder + ACV for secondary.

techniques.name: Psyllium + xanthan combination
techniques.rationale: Psyllium provides elasticity; xanthan provides gas-trapping film. Together they cover more of gluten's functions.

techniques.name: Coconut flour hydration rest
techniques.rationale: Coconut flour absorbs moisture for 5-10 minutes after mixing. Rest prevents over-thickening after folding in whites.

research.strategy: Multi-source food science compilation from peer-reviewed papers, professional baking resources, and GF baking community expertise
